name: Primary Venture Partners
identity_check: Confirmed as Primary Venture Partners (primary.vc; site operated by Primary Venture Management, LLC per its terms of use; press also writes 'Primary' or 'Primary Ventures'), the New York seed firm Ben Sun and Brad Svrluga co-founded in 2015. The approach page lists HQ NYC, stage 'Inception to Seed', current fund $625M and AUM $1.6B; TechCrunch (2018, 2021, 2026) and Forbes (2022) describe the same firm and fund sequence. Not Prime Venture Partners (the Indian seed fund), not Primary Capital or Primary Group, and not unrelated 'Primary' funds; 'Primary Select' is its own opportunity-fund series.

thesis_text.value: Self-described specialized, scaled seed firm that leads pre-seed and seed rounds across tech through partner-run sector practices: financial services and enterprise AI, healthcare, vertical AI, compute/infrastructure, cybersecurity, consumer, GTM tech and industrials. It makes few, concentrated bets (2-3 per partner a year) and backs them with a 60+ person operating team and an incubation arm, PrimaryLabs.

open_items: No application form or apply URL: the home page only has a 'Get in touch' mailto to a generic founders@ address (not recorded). Cold inbound inferred from that and the co-founders' letter on /approach.

Nothing stated on Indian founders or on requiring a US entity. The approach page says 'Investing Everywhere'; Fund V post mentions founders 'from San Francisco to Tel Aviv', and the portfolio includes Tel Aviv-based Atero (acquired by Crusoe).

No total portfolio count published. Fund V post says 9 of the 25 Fund I investments became unicorns; TechCrunch (2026) says Fund V plans 40-50 companies over three years and had made three investments.
SEC EDGAR refused the declared User-Agent (403), so Form D filings (legal fund names, exact sizes, close dates) were not checked. Fund close dates are announcement dates.
Fund V: $625M 'across two new funds' (Dow Jones) / 'fifth set of funds'; the split between the core seed fund and the second vehicle is not disclosed. Select Fund I (size, date) not found.
AUM: $1.6B (primary.vc/approach) vs $1.65B (TechCrunch 2026); not a schema field.

Partner titles differ by page: /people lists Jason Shuman 'Partner, Physical AI', Cassie Young 'Partner, Enterprise AI', Brian Schechter 'Partner, Compute'; /approach shows 'Partner, Vertical AI', 'Partner, GTM Tech', 'Partner, Infrastructure'. Recorded /people titles. Focus sectors are classified from bios. Industrials juniors: Devon Pasieka (Associate, Industrials), Adam Piasecki (Senior Associate, Physical AI).
stated_sectors mapping: Cybersecurity and GTM Tech mapped to enterprise_saas; the 'Physical AI' practice to robotics_physical_ai; the 2025 energy expansion to climate_energy.

Haiqu seed date (2025-01-14) comes only from the primary.vc post date, which is unreliable on the rebuilt site (see conflicts). Lyric seed, Bobyard seed, LightTable pre-seed and 1mind seed are dated by year only (Primary's 'Invested' year or 'spring of 2024'); exact announcement dates not found.

Rounds seen but not recorded: Tabs $55M Series B led by Lightspeed (date not verified); 1mind $30M Series A led by Battery (Primary's participation not explicit; date not verified); Bedrock Ocean $25M (stage not stated, date unverified); Teleskope $25M with M13 and Lerer (stage not stated); Circuit & Chisel seed with ParaFi (amount not stated); ExploreTech pre-seed 2025 (amount not found); Cargado/Cordage, Ply, Gryps (no round page fetched); healthcare deals EZ Health $26M (2026-09), Tokaido Health $25M (2026-05), Valerie Health $30M Series A; Etched Series C.
No street address published on primary.vc; terms page gives New York governing law and NYC courts.
